data: Machines were available 99.62% of scheduled hours. Downtime cost 5,021 machine-hours and about $90,663 of theo (0.39% of all theo).
Lost theo valued at each machine's own theo per available hour in that month (not floor average), so busy machines count more than quiet ones.
Upper bound: some players just move to another machine when one is down. Assumes an outage hour is an average hour.
Repair tickets explain 98.3% of downtime; every downtime hour matches an operations ticket (0 'unexplained' machine-days). 28% of fault downtime is waiting for a technician, not repairing.
1207 faults; avg wait 1.14 h, avg fix 2.95 h
Reconciled machine_day (scheduled - available seconds) against ticket intervals split at the 06:00 gaming-day boundary.
Ticket open time is when the machine became unavailable; faults nobody noticed would not appear.
Ridgeline machines fail most: 4.04 faults per 100 machine-days (95% CI 3.73-4.34) vs Northwind 1.67.
Rates per machine-day on the floor, not raw counts, so a brand with more machines is not penalized.
Manufacturer overlaps with game title and age; this is association, not proof the brand causes faults.
Downtime was worst in 2025-05 (1,009 machine-hours, avg wait 2.22 h vs 1.14 h overall) and the grave shift waits 1.96 h for a tech vs 0.90 h on day shift; repair time is the same on every shift.
grave 1.96 h, swing 0.85 h, day 0.90 h
Repair (fix) time compared by shift too: it barely changes, so the gap is staffing/response, not harder faults.
Shift assigned by ticket open time; long outages span shifts.

Adding one technician (best case: grave shift) would recover about $513 of theo in the 30-day window (range $128-$769) for $11,520. Preventive maintenance: $-125 for $9,000. Downtime is real but too cheap to fix with this budget.
benefit < cost for both downtime actions
Tried each shift and the worst manufacturer; valued hours with the time-of-day profile of play.
Theo is expected win, not profit; ignores guest goodwill from fewer dead machines.

data: Machines were available 99.62% of scheduled hours. Downtime cost 5,021 machine-hours and about $90,663 of theo (0.39% of all theo).
Lost theo valued at each machine's own theo per available hour in that month (not floor average), so busy machines count more than quiet ones.
Upper bound: some players just move to another machine when one is down. Assumes an outage hour is an average hour.
Repair tickets explain 98.3% of downtime; every downtime hour matches an operations ticket (0 'unexplained' machine-days). 28% of fault downtime is waiting for a technician, not repairing.
1207 faults; avg wait 1.14 h, avg fix 2.95 h
Reconciled machine_day (scheduled - available seconds) against ticket intervals split at the 06:00 gaming-day boundary.
Ticket open time is when the machine became unavailable; faults nobody noticed would not appear.
Ridgeline machines fail most: 4.04 faults per 100 machine-days (95% CI 3.73-4.34) vs Northwind 1.67.
Rates per machine-day on the floor, not raw counts, so a brand with more machines is not penalized.
Manufacturer overlaps with game title and age; this is association, not proof the brand causes faults.
Downtime was worst in 2025-05 (1,009 machine-hours, avg wait 2.22 h vs 1.14 h overall) and the grave shift waits 1.96 h for a tech vs 0.90 h on day shift; repair time is the same on every shift.
grave 1.96 h, swing 0.85 h, day 0.90 h
Repair (fix) time compared by shift too: it barely changes, so the gap is staffing/response, not harder faults.
Shift assigned by ticket open time; long outages span shifts.

Adding one technician (best case: grave shift) would recover about $513 of theo in the 30-day window (range $128-$769) for $11,520. Preventive maintenance: $-125 for $9,000. Downtime is real but too cheap to fix with this budget.
benefit < cost for both downtime actions
Tried each shift and the worst manufacturer; valued hours with the time-of-day profile of play.
Theo is expected win, not profit; ignores guest goodwill from fewer dead machines.
The comp program cost $190,669 (Jan-Jun), already inside the $937,936 POS cost of goods; guests saw $682,750 of menu value.
player_period comp cost matches property_day comp cost to the cent; counted once.
Only carded play earns points; comp cost is house cost, not menu price.
On 2025-05-01 the point price of comps was cut overnight: 13.1 -> 5.8 points per comp dollar (-56%). Comp cost per $1,000 carded theo rose from $11.95 to $13.09 (95% CI of change +0.65 to +1.67).
30 days either side only (less seasonality): cost per $1k theo change +0.55 (CI -0.06 to +1.16). Daily block bootstrap by week.
No control group: the change was floor-wide, so other May events can't be fully ruled out.
Making comps cost fewer points did not bring more carded play: carded theo per day changed -1.6% (95% CI $-4,009 to $+1,288 per day).
Checked the 30-day window around the change as well.
Two months after; long-run loyalty effects unknown. A randomized pilot would settle it.

Platinum comp cost per month went from $2,629 to $8,442 while Gold fell $17,203 -> $14,682: more players are reaching Platinum (tiers use lifetime points), so tier mix is a second driver of comp cost.
Split by tier at month end so the rate change and tier creep are not confused.
Tier is the tier after the player's last event that month.

Checked by tier and age band to see if one group drives it
Carded play only; uncarded players are not visible
The comp program cost $190,669 (Jan-Jun), already inside the $937,936 POS cost of goods; guests saw $682,750 of menu value.
player_period comp cost matches property_day comp cost to the cent; counted once.
Only carded play earns points; comp cost is house cost, not menu price.
On 2025-05-01 the point price of comps was cut overnight: 13.1 -> 5.8 points per comp dollar (-56%). Comp cost per $1,000 carded theo rose from $11.95 to $13.09 (95% CI of change +0.65 to +1.67).
30 days either side only (less seasonality): cost per $1k theo change +0.55 (CI -0.06 to +1.16). Daily block bootstrap by week.
No control group: the change was floor-wide, so other May events can't be fully ruled out.
Making comps cost fewer points did not bring more carded play: carded theo per day changed -1.6% (95% CI $-4,009 to $+1,288 per day).
Checked the 30-day window around the change as well.
Two months after; long-run loyalty effects unknown. A randomized pilot would settle it.

Platinum comp cost per month went from $2,629 to $8,442 while Gold fell $17,203 -> $14,682: more players are reaching Platinum (tiers use lifetime points), so tier mix is a second driver of comp cost.
Split by tier at month end so the rate change and tier creep are not confused.
Tier is the tier after the player's last event that month.
